Short-period comets have orbital periods of less than 200 years. This is a key characteristic that helps us narrow down their origin.

The Kuiper belt is a region of icy bodies beyond Neptune's orbit. It is thought to be the source of many short-period comets. The Kuiper belt is in the plane of the solar system, which means that short-period comets tend to originate from this region.

The asteroid belt is a region between Mars and Jupiter where many asteroids are found. While some short-period comets may originate from the asteroid belt, this is not the primary source of short-period comets.

The Oort cloud is a distant, spherical shell of icy bodies surrounding the solar system. It is thought to be the source of long-period comets, not short-period comets.
